programme: No single module spans these twelve factors. They split into disconnected sub-groups: a neural-stem-cell/neurogenesis axis (NR2E1/TLX, with HOXA11 acting through injury-induced HOXA11-AS), a systemic glucocorticoid-stress-response factor whose target list is dominated by classic hepatic and inflammatory glucocorticoid-response genes (NR3C1 → PCK1, CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, SERPINE1, IL6, NFKBIA, RELA), a MYC-MAX-antagonist/cell-cycle-brake cluster converging on RB1-E2F-cyclin-CDKN targets (MNT, E2F8, ZBTB7A → CCND1/CCND2/CDKN1A/CDKN2A/RB1/TP53/MDM2/MAX/TERT), a chromatin-architecture factor (CTCF), a liver-lineage cell-cycle repressor (ZHX2 → AFP/CCNA2/CCNE1/GPC3/HNF1A) and two immune-tolerance factors (AIRE, AKNA) sharing targets with nothing else here. None of these sub-clusters is carried by more than two or three factors with independent literature placement, and no complex or pathway ties the sub-clusters to one another.
role_in_a: Essentially undemonstrated in this record. CTCF's only hit is a pan-cancer study of insulated-neighbourhood disruption, not liver-cancer-specific; ZHX2 would classically be expected to repress AFP/CCNA2/CCNE1 in hepatocytes, but no retrieved paper places it in Liver_Cancer, and Open Targets records no association for any of the twelve factors in this disease.
role_in_b: Three separate, non-overlapping CNS mechanisms rather than one pathway: NR2E1/TLX drives post-stroke neural stem cell proliferation via Wnt/beta-catenin signalling; NR3C1 mediates post-stroke neuroinflammation and pyroptosis; HOXA11-AS regulates ischemic neuronal death via a miR-337-3p/YBX1 axis. These do not converge on a common downstream programme.
shared_axis: No documented or mechanistically plausible shared axis emerges. The closest candidate is NR3C1 as a systemic glucocorticoid-stress mediator active in both liver metabolism and post-stroke neuroinflammation, but this is a single factor's dual tissue role, not a shared multi-factor programme, and nothing in the record links it to the other eleven factors or to Liver_Cancer specifically.
reasoning: The twelve factors have no common target set, no shared complex, and no pathway description that would justify calling them a module; the cell-cycle-brake reading (MNT/E2F8/ZBTB7A/CTCF/ZHX2) is the kind of generic 'many transcription factors touch CCND1/CDKN1A' story the task explicitly warns against. Liver_Cancer support is essentially absent for all twelve factors, stroke support is confined to three factors acting through unrelated CNS mechanisms, and several literature hits are likely false positives on gene-symbol collisions (MNT as 'medical nutrition therapy', AKNA in an unrelated toxin review, ZHX2 papers on kidney/breast cancer only) per the reader's notes.
support: PMID 37059588 — HOXA11-AS regulates ischemic neuronal death (stroke only, not liver). PMID 39596503 — TLX/NR2E1 promotes stroke-induced neurogenesis (stroke only). PMID 20010817 — TLX/NR2E1 activates Wnt/beta-catenin in neural stem cell proliferation (stroke only). PMID 41949581 — NR3C1 regulates pyroptosis/neuroinflammation after stroke (stroke only). PMID 41675054 — NR3C1-linked circRNA regulates neural stem cell proliferation/differentiation (stroke only). PMID 31945090 — CTCF-bound insulated neighbourhoods altered pan-cancer, including liver cancer, but not stroke (liver only, not disease-specific). PMID 41372159 — TET1-based in vivo methylome editing demonstrated in liver tissue, a methods paper, not a liver-cancer disease link. None of these jointly connect Liver_Cancer and Stroke.
how_to_falsify: Perturb NR3C1, NR2E1, and CTCF individually (knockdown/knockout) in a hepatocellular carcinoma model and in an ischemic stroke model, then compare the transcriptional response of each factor's own target list (e.g. PCK1/IL6/SERPINE1 for NR3C1) across the two tissue contexts. If a shared axis truly existed, perturbing these factors should shift a correlated signature in both liver and brain; independent, non-overlapping responses in each tissue would confirm that the factors act through unrelated, tissue-specific programmes rather than a shared mechanism, consistent with the incoherent verdict here.
caveats: Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 30 patient-group comparisons (blood|liver tissue pairing), so replication is modest despite the high recurrence fractions. The single-view exclusions (ZBTB4, MEF2C, CIITA, CREB5, PURB, PEG3) and tissue-generic exclusions (RORA, MEF2C, HLX, CREB5, CIITA, VDR, RELB, IRF1, SPI1, DNMT1, PRDM1, SPIB) were correctly removed before ranking, so the absence of obvious immune/inflammatory master regulators from the surviving list is by design, not an oversight. The overall record explicitly notes no good evidence for any of these factors in Liver_Cancer and thin, mechanistically unrelated evidence for Stroke — this pair should not be over-interpreted as a positive finding.
